source.title: Extending AdamW by Leveraging Its Second Moment and Magnitude
source.authors: Guoqiang Zhang; Niwa Kenta; W. Kleijn

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Compares a new adaptive optimizer with AdamW on validation performance in two deep-learning tasks, bearing on optimizer-related generalization, but it does not test the claim versions' specified comparisons with SGD or their other conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-accuracy comparisons between Aida and AdamW. Its toy optimization experiments report optimization behavior rather than held-out generalization. The paper does not test the supplied claim versions as written.
record.test_reason: The introduction cites SGD's advantage over adaptive optimizers, but the study compares only adaptive optimizer settings. It does not compare adaptive methods with SGD, test recovery through weight decay or switching, or test any other supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: Aida (1,2) improves validation accuracy over the Adam-equivalent setting on both tested deep-learning tasks, while suitable exponent settings depend on the optimization problem.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates Aida, an extension of AdamW with additional parameters p and q; its deep-learning comparisons use Adam-equivalent Aida settings as the reference. The paper does not reproduce the supplied claim versions' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: On Swin-Transformer over CIFAR10, the reported Adam-equivalent validation accuracy differs between β2 = 0.98 and β2 = 0.999.

fits_no_version.finding: On WMT16 translation, Aida (1,2) achieved 67.8±0.28 validation accuracy versus Adam's 64.76±0.63, with similar training-loss trajectories. On CIFAR-10, corresponding accuracies at beta2=0.98 were 89.25±0.29 and 85.86±0.23; Adam at beta2=0.999 achieved 78.23±2.52.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the adaptive update exponents improves validation accuracy over the tested Adam settings on these two Transformer tasks.

record.problems: The deep-learning evaluation reports validation accuracy but not training accuracy, so the training-test gap is unavailable. The comparisons use three experimental repetitions per setup. The paper does not compare with SGD or momentum SGD.
record.rows_left_out: No held-out performance rows were left out. The toy optimization results in Fig. 4 concern gradient-norm convergence on optimization objectives, not test error or generalization.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; recovery through decoupled weight decay or switching; word-level language modeling.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and their dependence on data size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: The relevant failure to test V4 is the absent SGD comparison, not an unavailable training-test accuracy gap. The paper's local stability analysis concerns optimization dynamics, not V7's empirical relationship between weight-perturbation sharpness and generalization.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and architectural bias.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited tuning; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay or optimizer switching; word-level language models.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error and its interaction with training-set size, data augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measured properties as predictors of the training-test gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and subsequent test accuracy.
